Recode the Values of a Column

Source: R/figure-data.R
PlotDataRecode.Rd

Maps the values of a column to new values. Each value is looked up, in this order, in an exact map, in a list of regular expressions (patterns, the first match wins) and by position in index (integer codes counted from index_base); an optional extract expression first picks the part of each value that is looked up. Unmatched values are kept, or replaced by default. Finally substitute applies regular-expression replacements to every value, in order (for example to turn analysis names into display labels).

Usage

PlotDataRecode(
  data,
  column,
  map = NULL,
  patterns = NULL,
  index = NULL,
  index_base = 0L,
  extract = NULL,
  default = NULL,
  keep_unmatched = is.null(default),
  substitute = NULL,
  into = column
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

column

Column to recode.

map

Optional named vector or list: old value to new value.

patterns

Optional named vector or list: regular expression to new value, tried in order for values not in map.

index

Optional names for integer codes: a vector, or a data frame whose first column is used.

index_base

Code of the first name of index.

extract

Optional regular expression with one capture group; the group is looked up instead of the whole value.

default

Value for unmatched entries; NULL keeps them.

keep_unmatched

Keep unmatched values; with FALSE they become default (missing when default is NULL).

substitute

Optional list of c(pattern, replacement) pairs (Perl regular expressions) applied to every value at the end, in order.

into

Name of the result column; default column.

Value

data with the recoded column.

Details

The result is numeric when every replacement value is numeric and unmatched values are not kept (for example ordinal codes for reported categories); otherwise it is text.

See also

Other plot-data builders: PlotDataBindRows(), PlotDataConstant(), PlotDataCount(), PlotDataCrossShares(), PlotDataDirection(), PlotDataDominant(), PlotDataFromArrays(), PlotDataJoin(), PlotDataKeyColours(), PlotDataLabels(), PlotDataLonger(), PlotDataMembership(), PlotDataPairRatio(), PlotDataProduct(), PlotDataQuantiles(), PlotDataRankRows(), PlotDataRatio(), PlotDataRelative(), PlotDataSelect(), PlotDataShares(), PlotDataSummarise(), PlotDataUnite()

Examples

d <- data.frame(e = c("pct|B cells", "density|B cells"), g = c("A-x", "B"), cn = c(0, 2))
PlotDataRecode(d, "e", substitute = list(c("^pct\\|(.*)$", "\\1 (% of cells)"),
                                         c("^density\\|(.*)$", "\\1 (per mm2)")))
#>                      e   g cn
#> 1 B cells (% of cells) A-x  0
#> 2    B cells (per mm2)   B  2
PlotDataRecode(d, "g", patterns = c("^A" = "first"), default = "other", into = "label")
#>                 e   g cn label
#> 1     pct|B cells A-x  0 first
#> 2 density|B cells   B  2 other
PlotDataRecode(d, "cn", index = c("zero", "one", "two"), into = "name")
#>                 e   g cn name
#> 1     pct|B cells A-x  0 zero
#> 2 density|B cells   B  2  two
PlotDataRecode(data.frame(tps = c("0", "<1", "8", "n.a.")), "tps",
               map = list("0" = 0, "<1" = 0.5, "8" = 8), keep_unmatched = FALSE, into = "score")
#>    tps score
#> 1    0   0.0
#> 2   <1   0.5
#> 3    8   8.0
#> 4 n.a.    NA
